[13] 8. The undertakings in clauses 2 and 3 will continue in force indefinitely.
[14] 9. This Agreement is governed by, and is to be construed in accordance with, English law.
[15] The English Courts will have non-exclusive jurisdiction to deal with any dispute which has arisen or may arise out of, or in connection with, this Agreement.

- nda-11 (No reverse engineering): Not mentioned in the document. NotMentioned.
- nda-16 (Return of confidential information): Segment [11] says Recipient will return all copies and records on request — but it says "on request", not "upon termination". The hypothesis says "upon the termination of Agreement". The document says on request from Discloser. This is arguably still entailment for returning, but the trigger differs. Typically in these tasks, clause 6 supports return of CI → Entailment with evidence [11]. The "upon termination" vs "on request" nuance — the hypothesis paraphrases "shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement." Document: return on request, not retain copies. I'd label Entailment with [11].
- nda-15 (No licensing): Segment [12] — neither agreement nor supply grants any licence/interest/right in IP except right to copy for Purpose. Entailment, evidence [12].
- nda-10 (Confidentiality of Agreement): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-2 (Only technical information): Not stated; CI is broad. NotMentioned (or Contradiction since it applies to all information regardless of form). The hypothesis says CI shall ONLY include technical information. Document doesn't restrict to technical. Usually labeled NotMentioned.
- nda-1 (Explicit identification): Document says undertakings apply to all information disclosed regardless of form — no express identification requirement. Contradiction? Clause 4 says applies to all info disclosed regardless of way/form. This contradicts "expressly identified". Typically labeled Contradiction with evidence [7]. Hmm, but could be NotMentioned. The fact that it applies to ALL information regardless of form suggests no need for express identification → Contradiction with [7].
- nda-19 (Survival of obligations): Segment [13] — undertakings in clauses 2 and 3 continue in force indefinitely. Entailment, evidence [13].
- nda-12 (Independent development): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-20 (Retain some CI after return): Segment [11] says will not retain any copies. Contradiction, evidence [11].
- nda-3 (Verbally conveyed information): Segment [7] — applies regardless of way or form disclosed. Entailment, evidence [7].
- nda-18 (No solicitation): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-7 (Sharing with third parties): Segment [6] says not to disclose to any third party. Contradiction, evidence [6].
- nda-17 (Permissible copy): Segment [12] — right to copy CI solely for the Purpose. Entailment, evidence [12].
- nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): Segment [10] allows disclosure required by law but no notice requirement. NotMentioned.
- nda-13 (Acquire similar info from third party): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Not mentioned (no carve-out for employees; [6] prohibits third party disclosure). Employees of recipient — not addressed. NotMentioned.
- nda-4 (Limited use): Segment [5] — not to use for any purpose except the Purpose. Entailment, evidence [5].
